name: Guest feedback, reviews and complaints (the operator's record of what the public said, and what was said back)
one_line: The one situation in the trading family whose characteristic artefact is AUTHORED BY A MEMBER OF THE PUBLIC and answered by the operator: a platform review export with a management-response column, a satisfaction or NPS instrument fired at people who actually transacted, a direct complaint with its acknowledgement, investigation note, redress decision and closure, and the goodwill log that records what was paid to make it go away. Its structural inversion is the whole point - every other template in this schema holds what the OPERATOR wrote about a guest, and this row holds what a GUEST wrote about the operator, plus the reply. It is recognised by a DUAL DATE (the visit or stay, distinct from the date of writing) bound to a BOUNDED-SCALE RATING or a grievance, a CHANNEL slot, and above all a RESPONSE PAIRED TO A SPECIFIC THIRD-PARTY UTTERANCE. It is not the survey shape and not the word `review`: a mystery-shopper report, an employee engagement survey, a competitor-benchmark scrape and a hygiene rating all wear this shape and none of them is this row. A PLACEHOLDER TEMPLATE: it writes NO field rows and recommends NO folder dimensions, because the retail_hospitality schema declares none (PR-6, D1 as narrowed).

proposed_fields.example: where the utterance was made and where the reply must go - `Google`, `Tripadvisor`, `Booking.com`, `Trustpilot`, `direct email`, `comment card`, `post-stay survey`
proposed_fields.why_no_existing_key: THE ONE MINT THIS ROW ASKS FOR, and it asks because the schema's own `site` proposal cannot carry it without breaking. That proposal explicitly folds an e-commerce channel into `site` - `Shopify - UK store` - on the reading that a channel is a trading unit. That reading holds for SELLING (the operator does trade from Shopify) and fails completely for FEEDBACK (the operator does not trade from Tripadvisor). A single-site hotel has ONE trading unit and FIVE review channels; if channel is a `site` value, those five collapse into one branch and the operator loses the only dimension that governs their actual workflow, since response obligations, character limits, right of reply, moderation rules and takedown routes are all properties of the PLATFORM and of nothing else. No canonical key covers it: `venue` and `institution` are places and bodies, `record_type` and `work_type` are function values, `download_session` is a retrieval clue, `authored_by` is the reviewer and is never destination-eligible. HONEST COUNTER-CASE, recorded rather than smoothed: `channel` could be read as a MEDIUM, and a medium is one of the things a row may not be built on. This row's answer is that the key is not proposed as the row's identity - the row's identity is the paired utterance-and-response structure - and that a platform is a counterparty with rules, not a file format. If R1c disagrees, the correct outcome is that this row has no second dimension at all and recommends `site` alone, NOT that `site` is stretched to swallow platforms. Deliberately NOT minted alongside it: `rating`, `sentiment`, `nps_score`, `complaint_category`, `platform`, `reviewer` - the first three are derived measures rather than organizing facts, the fourth is a synonym of this key, and the fifth is a member of the public and constitutionally never a folder level.
proposed_fields.rule_family: labelled-slot plus gazetteer-with-context (R4 owns any platform-name list; this row writes none) - a column or field literally headed Source, Channel, Platform, Site or Review site, or an export whose own manifest or header block names the originating service. A platform name loose in free text is never sufficient, because a review body routinely names a rival platform.

deterministic: PRECONDITION on every entry below, and it is stricter for this row than for any of its thirteen siblings: each entry is a DETECTION signal and never an extraction licence. The schema declares no field rows, so nothing here writes a domain fact. Detection exists so the material is recognised, kept local, and offered honestly - and the material here is third-party authored content about named private individuals on both sides. “Privacy policy must be enforced before content reaches any model or external connector.”

THE PAIRED UTTERANCE-AND-RESPONSE structure, and it is this row's first and strongest signal because no other template in this schema produces it. A tabular or per-item record in which a FREE-TEXT PASSAGE ATTRIBUTED TO A NAMED OR DISPLAY-NAMED THIRD PARTY is set beside an OPERATOR REPLY in its own slot - Management response, Owner response, Reply, Response date. The second column is the discriminator: a survey tool collects, it does not answer. “Spreadsheets such as XLSX, XLS, CSV, TSV, ODS, and Numbers exports should yield workbook or file metadata, sheet names, column headers, visible cell values, table-like regions, formulas only when useful, and dates or identifiers from labeled cells.”

THE DUAL-DATE structure. Two distinct labelled dates that are NOT a created-and-modified pair: a DATE OF EXPERIENCE (date of stay, date of visit, dined on, order date) and a DATE OF WRITING (posted, submitted, published, received). Every other record in this family carries ONE operative date, because a trading record is made at the moment it records. Feedback is made afterwards, and the gap between the two dates is the row's cleanest deterministic tell.

A BOUNDED-SCALE RATING WITH ITS MAXIMUM STATED - out of five, out of ten, a star count, a 1-5 legend sheet, a Likert anchor row (Strongly disagree to Strongly agree), or a recommend-to-a-friend 0-10 with a promoter/passive/detractor derivation beside it. The stated maximum matters: an unbounded numeric column is a quantity or a price and belongs to a sibling.

THE QUESTION-BANK-AND-RESPONSE-MATRIX structure of a satisfaction instrument: one column per question with the question text as the header, one row per respondent, a scale legend held separately, a free-text `anything else` column, and usually a partial-completion pattern down the right-hand side. This is a research instrument shape, which is exactly why it collides - see collides_with for the discriminators against employee engagement and against market research.

THE ESCALATION-AND-CLOSURE chain of a direct complaint, read across several files or several messages in one thread: an inbound grievance, a dated acknowledgement, an internal investigation or account-of-events note, a REDRESS DECISION (refund, voucher, comped item, goodwill gesture, points, replacement) with a value and an authoriser, and a closing letter or final-response paragraph. The chain, not any one member, is the signal; a single apology email is not this structure.

A REDRESS LEDGER: one row per incident with a date, an issue category drawn from a short fixed list, a redress type, a monetary or points VALUE, and an authorising initial or name. Money in cells does not make it finance - see never_alone - and the discriminator against a refunds ledger is that this record is keyed to a GRIEVANCE and its category, whereas a refunds ledger is keyed to a RETURN AUTHORISATION and a stock movement.

A record whose SUBJECT IS A SITE THE HOLDER OPERATES and whose AUTHOR IS NOT THE HOLDER. This pairing is what separates the row's genuine material from the three most convincing false positives at once: a competitor-benchmark scrape fails the first half, an employee engagement survey fails on subject (the workplace, not the trading offer), and a mystery-shopper report fails the second half because the assessor was instructed by the holder.

An email or message thread whose labelled subject slot carries a grievance or feedback term together with an ORDER, BOOKING, STAY or CASE reference, and whose body contains a request for a remedy. The reference-plus-remedy pairing is what fires. A hospitality-sounding sender domain alone does not, and a subject line reading `Feedback` alone does not.

A scan or photograph of a paper COMMENT CARD or feedback slip - a printed prompt block, a tick-box or face scale, a handwritten comment, and often a name-and-contact block the guest filled in voluntarily. This family produces more photographed paper than any other in the roster and the handwriting is frequently the whole content. “A screenshot is always a screenshot of something—a receipt, application portal, conversation, code problem, document, calendar, or research figure—and without OCR the product sees only an image with a weak filename.”
An archive whose MANIFEST names a review or reputation export, a survey run, a feedback period or a case bundle - read from the manifest alone and not unpacked to improve classification.

Parent-folder context naming reputation, feedback, guest relations, complaints, customer care or a platform, treated as a clue that raises plausibility once one of the structures above is already present. Folder context never fires alone.
needs_llm: PRECONDITION: this row's ordinary output is unstructured natural-language grievance and praise written by members of the public, frequently naming staff. A model step runs under the user's policy and after P7. “Protected material should not be included in cloud-model prompts by default, should not display raw content in general group summaries, and should not be moved automatically without a user policy that explicitly permits it.”

WHOSE VOICE IS THIS - the row's central determination, and the one on which it should abstain most often. Four authors produce near-identical bytes: a GUEST evaluating the holder's site (this row), an INSTRUCTED ASSESSOR scoring the holder's site against a rubric (a standards audit), the HOLDER evaluating somebody else's site (not this schema at all, and not the operator's side), and a THIRD PARTY evaluating a COMPETITOR (market intelligence). Where the evidence does not settle authorship and subject together, this row must not activate.

WHOSE SIDE IS THIS, inherited from the schema and sharpened here. A review is published, so a copy of one can be held by anybody. The operator's copy carries a POPULATION or a RESPONSE APPARATUS - many reviews, a reply column, a case reference, an internal category. A single downloaded or screenshotted review carries neither.

Separating a LIVE feedback record from a TEMPLATE, a platform's own sample export, a training exercise, a supplier's demo of a reputation tool, or a blank comment card. A blank survey and a completed one are the same instrument with the answers removed. “Topic answers what a file is about, while purpose answers what the file was for.”

A purpose-coherent complaint packet whose members are individually unremarkable: the inbound letter, a photograph the guest attached, a screenshot of the booking, an internal note, a scan of the voucher issued and a closing reply. “The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent.”

Unlabelled operational prose - a drafted reply that quotes a review without citing it, a duty manager's account of an incident, a shift note recording that a table complained. These have no header block, no grid and no reference, and they are frequently the most sensitive files in the corpus because they narrate an allegation against a named colleague.

Recognising that a complaint has become an EMPLOYEE RELATIONS matter. The guest's letter is this row's; a witness statement, an investigation meeting invitation and an outcome letter about a named employee are not, however tightly they sit in the same folder.
Reading handwriting on a photographed comment card, where OCR confidence is low and the guest's contact details are frequently the most legible thing on it.

A review in a language whose praise, grievance, redress and hospitality vocabulary the deterministic structure catalogue does not cover - a materially larger share here than elsewhere in the family, because international guests review in their own language.
In every case above, abstention is the required outcome when evidence does not settle it. “A model that cannot cite sufficient evidence must return unknown.”
never_alone: THE WORD `REVIEW`, STANDING ALONE, and this row is required to answer it because its own schema names it: retail_hospitality's never_alone list reads `A DOCUMENT-TYPE WORD, standing alone - invoice, rota, log, price list, order, review`, and adds that a row resting on one is the schema's default template wearing a name. The answer is that `review` is the single most overloaded token this row could rest on - a licence review, a performance review, a code review, a design review, a literature review, a review of a book, a management review of a quality system, and `Review Later` the residual itself. `Review.docx` is nothing. What fires this row is never the word; it is the utterance-and-response pairing, the dual date, and the subject-is-my-site-author-is-not-me test.

A BOUNDED-SCALE RATING, STANDING ALONE. Five stars appear on an app-store listing, a supplier scorecard, an employee appraisal, a hygiene rating, a hotel's own star classification, a wine note and a film review. A rating column is a shape, and this row's schema is explicit that a shape without its labelled slots is not evidence.

A PLATFORM NAME, STANDING ALONE - Google, Tripadvisor, Trustpilot, Booking.com. Reviews routinely name rival platforms in their own text (`better than the place we found on Booking`), marketing decks name all of them, and a browser bookmark export names them all at once. The reasoning is read straight across from “A university name alone should not create a group because Columbia can appear as an authoring school, course provider, target institution, employer, research venue, or merely a cited organization.” - the sentence is about ROLE AMBIGUITY, and a platform name is worse, because it can be the channel, the subject, the tool, the competitor's channel or a passing mention.

A GUEST'S OR REVIEWER'S NAME OR DISPLAY NAME. This is the row's hardest rule and it is harder here than anywhere else in the family, because the reviewer's name is the most salient token in every single artefact this row holds. It must never anchor a group and must never become a folder level: the design warns the tree builder “when a level produces only one child, repeats a concept already expressed in the parent, creates excessive depth, or creates a large number of tiny folders”, and a branch per complainant is the purest possible instance of the last of those - as well as publishing a member of the public's name into the user's directory tree.

A NAMED MEMBER OF STAFF. The name in a complaint is the subject of an untested allegation. It is a literal observation and never a fact about that person, never a grouping anchor and never a dimension.

A SENTIMENT WORD OR AN EMOTIONAL REGISTER - `disappointed`, `disgusting`, `wonderful`, `never again`. Free-text affect is present in supplier disputes, HR grievances, personal correspondence and product returns alike, and a model reading tone rather than structure is exactly the failure mode the design's validation step exists to stop.
A DATE, STANDING ALONE, however feedback-shaped. Inherited from the schema: nearly every file in this world is dated. It is the PAIR of dates that fires here, never one.

A PHOTOGRAPH ATTACHED TO A COMPLAINT - a picture of a stained pillow, a wrong dish, a damaged item. It is `photos` evidence until the grievance structure around it claims it; an image of something unpleasant is not a complaint record.

work_types: platform review record - export, single review capture, response draft, response log, moderation or takedown request
solicited feedback record - post-stay or post-purchase survey instrument, results export, scale legend, comment card scan
direct complaint record - inbound grievance, acknowledgement, internal account of events, final response, closure
redress record - goodwill gesture note, voucher or comp authorisation, redress ledger row
reputation reporting record - period summary of scores, volumes and response rates across channels
testimonial and consent record - a quotation cleared for marketing use with the author's permission attached
grouping_reasons: ONE COMPLAINT CASE across its whole life: the inbound letter, the guest's attached photograph, an internal account of events, the redress authorisation and the final response - joined by a case, booking or order reference, NEVER by the complainant's name. Purpose-coherent even where the members share no content. “The documents are content-incoherent but purpose-coherent.”

ONE FEEDBACK PERIOD AT ONE SITE ON ONE CHANNEL: the export, the response log and the period summary for one quarter - and this is the reason most likely to be mis-drawn as a calendar, because every member is dated twice. The occasion is the reporting period AT A SITE AND CHANNEL; the year is not a grouping reason.
ONE SURVEY RUN: the instrument, the scale legend, the raw export and the summary deck - joined by the run's own name or its field dates.

One repeatedly re-exported platform dump, joined by the universal duplicate_family and version_family facts rather than by any trading fact. This family re-exports more than most, because a reputation export is regenerated every time a score is checked.

NOT A GROUPING REASON, and stated because it is the attractive wrong answer: the reviewer, the complainant or the staff member named in the complaint. A high-frequency person token acting as the only bridge is precisely what the design's stop rules exclude, and here it would also publish a private individual into the tree.

No group at all is a valid outcome and is COMMON here. A single screenshotted five-star review, one thank-you email, one comment card - these are isolated artefacts with no apparatus around them, and a residual's business rather than this row's.

template.why: EMPTY BY CONTRACT: PR-6 leaves the retail_hospitality schema with no field rows, and a dimension may only branch on a field the same schema declares. The recommendation is therefore held as prose, and it is stated here precisely because the node test requires this row to say how it differs from the schema's default - which reads: the TRADING UNIT only where the corpus spans more than one, then the TRADING OCCASION (session, count, order cycle, booking, function, licensed premises), then the OPERATIONAL RECORD FUNCTION, not time-first. THIS ROW DIFFERS AT THE MIDDLE LEVEL, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS REAL BUT IT IS PARTLY A SUBTRACTION - recorded honestly, not smoothed. For the row's highest-volume artefact, the platform export, the trading occasion COLLAPSES: platforms anonymise and do not return a booking reference, so most reviews cannot be tied to the stay that produced them, and a level the family default treats as its non-time top is simply unrecoverable. What should stand in its place is the CHANNEL - the platform an utterance was made on and must be answered on - because response obligations, right of reply, moderation and takedown are properties of the platform and of nothing else. That is why this row proposes `channel` and why it insists the schema's `site` cannot absorb it: a single-site hotel has one trading unit and five review channels, and folding them together destroys the only distinction the operator actually works by. The recommendation is therefore SITE (only where the corpus spans more than one) then CHANNEL then FEEDBACK RECORD FUNCTION, with the reporting period INSIDE, never above. NOT TIME-FIRST: this row is more tempted than most because its artefacts carry two dates each, and the answer is that both dates IDENTIFY the utterance rather than ROOT the tree - “For document and record domains, project, function, or subject usually comes before time because putting year first scatters related work across calendar folders.” - and the time-first licence belongs to capture-based media alone: “Photos and capture-based media are the major exception: time often belongs first because capture date is a defining aspect of the material.” A review is not a capture. THE ONE HALF OF THE MATERIAL THAT DOES KEEP THE OCCASION LEVEL is the direct complaint, which arrives with an order, booking or case reference; that internal split - export without an occasion, complaint with one - is recorded as an open question rather than resolved by fiat. TWO ABSOLUTE PROHIBITIONS, and they bind harder here than anywhere else in the family: a REVIEWER, COMPLAINANT OR GUEST must never become a dimension, and neither must a NAMED MEMBER OF STAFF - the first because the design warns against a level that creates “a large number of tiny folders” and because it would publish a member of the public into the directory tree, the second because it would file colleagues under untested allegations. A RATING must not become a dimension either: a five-star branch and a one-star branch are a sentiment sort, not an organizational fact. Any order remains editable - “The system recommends an order based on the domain template, but the user can reverse, remove, add, or flatten dimensions.”

collides_with.signal: SAME FIXTURE BOTH SIDES: `Satisfaction and NPS export Q1 2026.csv` - respondent identifier, a 0-10 recommend score, a free-text comment, a period. That row already authored this seam from its side, naming a premises, a booking or a guest-stay anchor as what supports this row; this entry states the reciprocal and names the same fixture. THIS ROW OWNS the export whose respondents are ONE-VISIT OR ANONYMOUS CONSUMERS keyed to a site, a stay, a table or an order reference, with a visit date distinct from the submission date. THAT ROW OWNS the export whose respondents are NAMED BUSINESS COUNTERPARTIES with an account, contract or subscription reference, a renewal date and a named account owner. Discriminated by the RESPONDENT-IDENTITY COLUMN: a booking or order reference decides for this row; an account or contract identifier with a relationship owner decides for that one. Neither may take the other on the 0-10 column alone. RETAIL_HOSPITALITY.GUEST-FEEDBACK MUST NOT TAKE a B2B account health review or a quarterly business review deck; BUSINESS_OPERATIONS.CUSTOMER-ACCOUNT-MANAGEMENT MUST NOT TAKE a platform review export merely because it contains satisfaction data.

SAME FIXTURE BOTH SIDES: `Reviews - competitor set - Q1 2026.xlsx` - ratings, comment text, dates and a platform column, exactly the shape of this row's canonical export. THIS ROW OWNS a record whose SUBJECT IS A SITE THE HOLDER OPERATES and whose author is not the holder, normally carrying a response column because a response is only possible on your own listing. THAT ROW OWNS a record assembled to answer a question about a MARKET - competitor sets, benchmark tables, sampled populations, a stated instrument or methodology, and no reply column anywhere because you cannot answer a rival's reviewer. Discriminated by the SUBJECT SITE plus the PRESENCE OR ABSENCE OF AN OPERATOR RESPONSE SLOT. RETAIL_HOSPITALITY.GUEST-FEEDBACK MUST NOT TAKE a benchmark scrape, a sentiment study or a category survey because it contains reviews; BUSINESS_OPERATIONS.MARKET-RESEARCH MUST NOT TAKE the holder's own reputation export because it can be read as a data set. AUTHORED ONE-WAY HERE; R1c owes the reciprocal.

SAME FIXTURE BOTH SIDES: `Re FW Complaint - order 55120 wrong size.eml`, a single thread carrying a grievance, an apology and a return authorisation number. THIS ROW OWNS THE UTTERANCE AND THE REPLY - the grievance text, the acknowledgement, the final response, and the goodwill gesture as a reputational act. THAT ROW OWNS THE GOODS-AND-MONEY MOVEMENT - the return authorisation number, the inbound receipt and inspection, the restocking or write-off, the refund or replacement, and a warranty claim onward to a manufacturer. Discriminated by THE RETURN AUTHORISATION AND ITS STOCK MOVEMENT: present, the record is that row's; absent, and with a case reference and a redress category instead, it is this row's. The same thread is legitimately split between them and neither should claim the whole of it. RETAIL_HOSPITALITY.GUEST-FEEDBACK MUST NOT TAKE an RA register, a refunds ledger or a warranty claim file; RETAIL_HOSPITALITY.RETURNS-WARRANTY MUST NOT TAKE a review, a survey export or a goodwill log keyed to grievance categories rather than to returned goods. AUTHORED ONE-WAY HERE; R1c owes the reciprocal.

SAME FIXTURE BOTH SIDES: `Guest history - Ashcroft.pdf` - one named guest, past stays with dates and room types, notes, preferences, and a `previous complaint - comped breakfast` line. THIS ROW OWNS THE POST-HOC EVALUATION AND ITS ANSWER: what the guest said about the stay and what was said back. THAT ROW OWNS CAPACITY AGAINST DATED DEMAND: the held slot, the party size, the requirements, the status and the no-show. Discriminated by WHETHER THE RECORD LOOKS FORWARD TO A SLOT OR BACKWARD AT AN EXPERIENCE - a dietary requirement is that row's, a complaint about the meal is this row's, and a guest-history sheet genuinely contains both. RETAIL_HOSPITALITY.GUEST-FEEDBACK MUST NOT TAKE a reservation sheet, an arrivals list or a preferences record; RETAIL_HOSPITALITY.BOOKINGS-RESERVATIONS MUST NOT TAKE a review export because its rows carry stay dates. Note for both: the guest's NAME is the bridge and is forbidden as a grouping anchor on both sides. AUTHORED ONE-WAY HERE; R1c owes the reciprocal.

SAME FIXTURE BOTH SIDES: `Mystery shopper report - Store 214 - Feb 2026.pdf`, this row's collision fixture - a visit date, a site, a score and a narrative, which is the guest-feedback shape almost exactly. THIS ROW OWNS the utterance of a person who came as a CUSTOMER, unbidden or solicited after the fact, evaluated against nothing but their own expectation. THAT ROW OWNS the STANDARDS AUDIT - an assessor instructed by the operator, scoring the site against an operator-defined rubric with points available and a pass mark, on an assignment or wave reference. Discriminated by THE RUBRIC AND WHO INSTRUCTED THE ASSESSOR: a scoring framework the operator wrote decides for that row; a free evaluation from a paying customer with a channel and a right of reply decides for this one. RETAIL_HOSPITALITY.GUEST-FEEDBACK MUST NOT TAKE a mystery-shop report, a brand-standards score or a site visit report; RETAIL_HOSPITALITY.STORE-OPERATIONS MUST NOT TAKE a review export because it scores the site. AUTHORED ONE-WAY HERE; R1c owes the reciprocal.

SAME FIXTURE BOTH SIDES: `Complaint - rude service, table 12, 14 Mar.pdf` - a guest's letter naming a member of staff. THIS ROW OWNS IT WHILE IT IS A GUEST-FACING MATTER: the grievance, the acknowledgement, the redress and the reply to the guest. HR OWNS THE EMPLOYEE RELATIONS PROCESS the letter may trigger: the investigation meeting invitation, witness statements, the outcome letter, the note on the personnel file. Discriminated by WHOSE PROCESS THE DOCUMENT BELONGS TO - addressed to the guest or about the employee. The seam is a MOMENT rather than a byte: identical folders hold both halves, and once a personnel process opens, hr's privacy posture governs the members that identify the employee even where this row's structure is what recognised the folder. RETAIL_HOSPITALITY.GUEST-FEEDBACK MUST NOT TAKE a disciplinary file, a witness statement or a performance note arising from a complaint; HR MUST NOT TAKE the guest's letter, the review, or the response sent to the complainant merely because a colleague is named in it. AUTHORED ONE-WAY HERE; R1c owes the reciprocal.

SAME FIXTURE BOTH SIDES: `Allergen incident - 6 Jun - guest reaction.docx` - a guest's reported reaction, the operator's reply, a batch code and a corrective action, all in one file. THIS ROW OWNS THE COMPLAINT AND THE RESPONSE TO THE COMPLAINANT. THAT ROW OWNS THE TRACEABILITY AND CORRECTIVE-ACTION CHAIN - which batch, which delivery, which check, what procedure changed, what was reported to an authority. Discriminated by WHETHER THE RECORD FACES THE GUEST OR FACES THE PROCESS. RETAIL_HOSPITALITY.GUEST-FEEDBACK MUST NOT TAKE a temperature log, a batch trace or a corrective-action register; RETAIL_HOSPITALITY.FOOD-SAFETY MUST NOT TAKE a complaint letter or a review that mentions illness. AUTHORED ONE-WAY HERE; R1c owes the reciprocal.

SAME FIXTURE BOTH SIDES: `Goodwill log 2026.xlsx` - dated rows, a monetary value column, an authoriser. FINANCE OWNS THE ACCOUNT AND THE LEDGER: an account identity, a posting or nominal code, a bookkeeping period, a credit note posted against a customer. THIS ROW OWNS THE REDRESS AS A SERVICE-RECOVERY ACT keyed to a grievance category and a case reference, with no account identity anywhere. Discriminated by THE PRESENCE OF AN ACCOUNT IDENTITY AND A POSTING STRUCTURE, the same discriminator the retail_hospitality schema authored against finance for takings, applied here to compensation. Where both are present the file is genuinely in both worlds and finance's protective ordering runs first, because finance is a safety schema. RETAIL_HOSPITALITY.GUEST-FEEDBACK MUST NOT TAKE a credit-note run, a chargeback settlement or a compensation provision in the accounts; FINANCE MUST NOT reduce a goodwill log to a payments list, because the grievance category it would discard is the reason the record exists. AUTHORED ONE-WAY HERE; R1c owes the reciprocal.

SAME FIXTURE BOTH SIDES: `Complaint - parcel arrived late and damaged - order 55120.eml`, a grievance whose subject is a delivery. THIS ROW OWNS THE CUSTOMER-FACING GRIEVANCE AND THE REPLY - the apology, the redress and the case closure. LOGISTICS OWNS THE CARRIAGE FAILURE AS A TRANSPORT RECORD - the consignment or tracking reference, the carrier claim, the proof-of-delivery dispute, the service-level credit. Discriminated by WHETHER THE RECORD IS KEYED TO A CONSIGNMENT OR TO A CUSTOMER CASE. RETAIL_HOSPITALITY.GUEST-FEEDBACK MUST NOT TAKE a carrier claim file or a delivery-performance report; LOGISTICS MUST NOT TAKE the customer's complaint or the reply sent to them. Thin but real, and included because the dispatch named logistics as a must-consider neighbour. AUTHORED ONE-WAY HERE; R1c owes the reciprocal.

falls_through_to.why: THE PRIMARY FALLTHROUGH FOR THIS ROW, and it is reached more often here than by most rows in the family, because the characteristic artefact names a private individual on one side and frequently a member of staff on the other. A complaint file, a review export carrying reviewer contact details, a scanned comment card with a name and a phone number, or an allergen-incident narrative all belong here when no accepted group is active. “Protected Records may represent sensitive isolated material such as passport scans, medical documents, account statements, visas, legal forms, or credentials; it should normally remain local-only and must not cause filenames or content to be exposed in model prompts.”

The cautious outcome for a feedback-shaped file whose AUTHOR, SUBJECT SITE or SIDE is unresolved - a ratings export whose subject may be a competitor, a scored visit report that may be a mystery shop, a survey that may be an employee instrument, or a scanned card whose handwriting OCR could not read. “Review Later may hold files whose meaning is partly understood but whose final location requires a future decision.”

The home for the single screenshotted review, which this world produces constantly and which carries no population and no response apparatus. “Temporary Screenshots may live under Photos/Temporary Screenshots and hold screenshots that appear time-sensitive or remind the user of something but have no accepted project, trip, application, or event relationship.” Positive screen-origin evidence is required first; a missing camera tag is not proof of a screenshot.

Named as a must-consider residual and it does apply, but narrowly: a durable standalone feedback-adjacent document with no case around it - a single thank-you letter kept for its own sake, a framed testimonial with a signed consent note, a one-off award certificate arising from guest voting. “Independent Records may live under Personal/Independent Records and hold standalone certificates, notices, confirmations, forms, and PDFs that have a durable purpose but no broader group.”

Named as a must-consider residual, and this row records honestly that it applies only at the edge, not at the centre. Its named material is transactional - “Receipts and Confirmations may hold isolated invoices, delivery confirmations, booking records, boarding passes, purchase receipts, event tickets, and similar transactional documents.” - and the artefact of this row that fits is the isolated REDRESS INSTRUMENT with no case around it: a lone voucher confirmation or refund confirmation email. The grievance that produced it is not a transactional document and does not belong here.

The safe outcome for a password-protected reputation-platform export or an unreadable survey-tool dump. “Unsupported or Encrypted may hold—or, more safely, represent without moving—password-protected archives, unreadable documents, damaged files, and unknown formats.”

sensitivity_why: THIS IS THE LEG THIS ROW PASSES MOST CLEARLY, and its posture is not merely inherited from the schema - it differs from the family default in three ways the schema's own paragraph does not contain. FIRST, THE LINKAGE TRAP, and it is the sharpest. This is the family's only material whose third-party personal data is SELF-PUBLISHED: a platform review was written by its author for the world to read, which makes it tempting to treat the local copy as low-risk. That inference is wrong and must be blocked. The operator's export is not the public page; it JOINS the public utterance to internal data that was never published - which booking it came from, which staff member was involved, what category it was filed under, what redress was paid and who authorised it. Public source, private linkage; and this row's copy is the linkage. The same trap has already been recorded once in this project by legal.practice-matter-file, which warns against deciding that a public filing makes the local file or the neighbouring packet low sensitivity, and the reasoning transfers exactly. SECOND, THE ALLEGATION AGAINST A NAMED COLLEAGUE. A complaint is, in substance, an untested accusation about an identified employee held in a trading folder rather than in a personnel system. It is employee-relations material arriving unbidden, it is frequently the most damaging file in the corpus to the person named, and it must never become a grouping anchor or a folder level - see the hr boundary and the never_alone rules. THIRD, SPECIAL-CATEGORY LEAKAGE THROUGH THE ORDINARY DOOR. Grievances routinely carry an accessibility need, an allergic reaction, an illness after a meal, a bereavement behind a cancellation, or an allegation of discriminatory treatment - health data and protected-characteristic data about named private individuals, arriving inside a routine operational export that nobody flagged as sensitive. Volume compounds all three: one review is an opinion, a year of reviews joined to booking references and staff names is a linked database about the public and the workforce at once. The design is therefore binding here: “Privacy policy must be enforced before content reaches any model or external connector.” and “Protected material should not be included in cloud-model prompts by default, should not display raw content in general group summaries, and should not be moved automatically without a user policy that explicitly permits it.” TWO HONESTY NOTES so this value is not read as more than it is. It does not invent a handling class - only none and potentially_sensitive are available in this phase and P7 owns the classes. And it does not claim every file here is sensitive: an anonymised period summary of scores, volumes and response rates carries no person at all. The posture exists because the safe and the sensitive members arrive inside the SAME export, and cannot be separated at recognition time.
open_question: Five, recorded rather than smoothed. NJ-GF-1 (the sharpest, and this row's own weakest point): THE COLLAPSED OCCASION LEVEL. The schema's default template puts a trading occasion between site and function, and for this row's highest-volume artefact - the platform export - that level is unrecoverable, because platforms anonymise and return no booking reference. Half this row's material therefore differs from the default by SUBTRACTION, which is uncomfortably close to a row defined by an absence. The row survives on its other two legs (detection and privacy) and on the fact that the DIRECT COMPLAINT half does keep an occasion reference, but R1c should decide explicitly: either this row's recommendation is site then channel then function (this pass's reading), or the row is split into an export-shaped situation and a case-shaped situation, or the occasion level is simply declared optional family-wide. NJ-GF-2: WHETHER `channel` IS A KEY OR A MEDIUM. This row's one proposal turns on a platform being a counterparty with rules rather than a delivery medium. If R1c reads it as a medium, the correct consequence is that this row recommends `site` alone and has no second dimension - NOT that the schema's `site` is stretched to swallow Tripadvisor, which would merge one hotel's five review channels into one branch. NJ-GF-3: THE MYSTERY-SHOP SEAM AS A GENERAL RULE. This pass discriminates guest voice from standards audit by the presence of an operator-authored RUBRIC and an instructed assessor. That rule may be wanted family-wide and beyond it - the same shape recurs as a supplier scorecard, a franchise brand-standards visit and a secret-diner programme. R1c should decide whether the rubric test belongs to this row, to retail_hospitality.store-operations, or to business_operations.compliance-audit, and all three should then say the same thing. NJ-GF-4: THE MOMENT A COMPLAINT BECOMES AN HR MATTER. The boundary authored above is a moment, not a byte, and no mechanism in the design decides moments. Alternatives: hr claims every file that names an employee in an allegation (safe, but strips the guest's own letter out of its case); this row keeps the guest-facing half and hr's privacy posture governs the employee-identifying members (this pass's reading); or the packet routes wholesale to Protected Records and neither row groups it. NJ-GF-5: THE PUBLIC-SOURCE PARADOX AS A PRODUCT RULE. Nothing in this phase can express `public content, private linkage`, and this row needs it more than any other in the family. Alternatives: P7 gains a linkage-aware class; the row's posture stays blanket potentially_sensitive and accepts over-protecting an anonymised score summary (this pass's reading); or the export is treated as ordinary and the linkage risk is accepted, which this row recommends against.
